Senses.Explanation: A reduplicated image built on "round" (圓): "round and rolling." It occurs 132 times in 81 allowlisted texts. The corpus repeatedly supplies concrete controls for the rendering. One line says it is "round and rolling, without edges or corners" (圓陀陀地無稜角). Another compares its movement to "a pearl running on a tray and a tray running around a pearl" and follows with "round and rolling, lively and active; emerging and disappearing, opening and folding, with nothing permitted or not permitted" (如盤走珠，如珠走盤，圓陀陀、活潑潑，出沒舒卷，無可不可). In a direct three-part exchange, "what is buddha?" receives "round and rolling" (圓陀陀), "what is the teaching?" receives "lively and active" (活潑潑), and "what is the monk?" receives "freely at ease" (任騰騰).
Senses.Note: Other predicates retain the same round, uncornered, mobile image. One verse pairs "round and rolling" with "shining and flashing" (圓陀陀，光爍爍), then says "large within large, narrow within narrow" (大中大，窄中窄). Another statement says, "round and rolling: never the least bit lacking, never the least bit in excess" (圓陀陀地，曾無一毫頭許欠少，曾無一毫頭許盈餘). The description is also criticized when made into a fixed stopping point: a later address says people take "the round-and-rolling, shining-and-flashing one" as the ultimate rule, while not knowing that it has no fixed body and that heading toward it goes astray (認著個圓陀陀、光爍爍的以為極則……無體性，趣向則乖). Productive forms include the adverbial "roundly and rolling" (圓陀陀地, 15 occurrences in 11 texts) and the exact light pairing "round and rolling, shining and flashing" (圓陀陀光爍爍, three in three).

Occurrences.Kwic: 傳家清白有風規。圓陀陀地無稜角。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Verse predicate: the inherited family is clean and white with its established style; round and rolling, without edges or corners.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：「如何是佛？」師云：「圓陀陀。」「如何是法？」師云：「活潑潑。」「如何是僧？」師云：「任騰騰。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Direct three-part answer: buddha is round and rolling; the teaching is lively and active; the monk is freely at ease.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如盤走珠，如珠走盤，圓陀陀、活潑潑，出沒舒卷，無可不可。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Concrete motion comparison: like a pearl running on a tray and the tray running around the pearl; round and rolling, lively and active.

Occurrences.Kwic: 後人認著個圓陀陀、光爍爍的以為極則
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Critical deployment: later people recognize the round-and-rolling, shining-and-flashing one as the ultimate rule. The following source text says it has no fixed body and heading toward it goes astray.

Occurrences.Kwic: 處世界，無所著，圓陀陀，光爍爍，大中大，窄中窄。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Verse line: dwelling in the world with nothing attached; round and rolling, shining and flashing; large within large, narrow within narrow.

Occurrences.Kwic: 圓陀陀地。曾無一毫頭許欠少。曾無一毫頭許盈餘。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Predicates the round-and-rolling form as lacking not the least bit and having not the least bit in excess.

RelatedTerms: pearl running on a tray (盤走珠)

Senses.Explanation: All at once or sudden (頓), plus to awaken (悟): to awaken all at once. The Platform Record gives the line that one's own nature awakens of itself, sudden awakening and sudden refining, with no gradual steps (自性自悟，頓悟頓修，亦無漸次). Its standing contrast is gradual (漸). A lamp record explains 'Southern sudden, Northern gradual' (南頓北漸) as a difference in how people are led to awaken, not as original north and south labels within Chan (開導發悟有頓漸之異，故曰南頓北漸，非禪宗本有南北之號也). In encounter narratives it appears in the formula 'awakened all at once at the words' (言下頓悟), where a recorded statement immediately precedes the awakening. Later Chinese Chan records pair sudden and gradual across awakening and refining. The Record of the Source-Mirror gives four propositions: gradual refining and sudden awakening, sudden awakening and gradual refining, gradual refining and gradual awakening, and sudden awakening and sudden refining (漸修頓悟 / 頓悟漸修 / 漸修漸悟 / 頓悟頓修). Another pairing states that principle must be awakened to all at once while affairs are removed gradually (理須頓悟，事在漸除). A Chinese Chan succession chart defines the term by saying that turning from delusion to awakening is sudden and turning an ordinary person into a sage is sudden awakening (從迷而悟即頓，轉凡成聖即頓悟也), then describes beginningless confusion that takes the four elements as the body and deluded thinking as the mind. Dazhu Huihai's book title also preserves the term: Treatise on the Essential Gate of Entering the Way by Sudden Awakening (頓悟入道要門論). The allowlist count is 878 hits in 183 texts; 'awakened all at once at the words' (言下頓悟) occurs 57 times, 'sudden awakening and gradual refining' (頓悟漸修) 14, and 'sudden awakening and sudden refining' (頓悟頓修) 13.
Senses.Note: A corpus-wide Chinese Chan term described through the sudden and gradual contrast (頓 / 漸). The entry distinguishes awakening all at once (頓悟) from refining all at once (頓修): the recorded phrase 'sudden awakening and gradual refining' (頓悟漸修) deliberately separates them. The evidence is limited to Chinese Chan texts and Chinese Chan discussions preserved in the allowlist.

Occurrences.Kwic: 自性自悟，頓悟頓修，亦無漸次，所以不立一切
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Platform Sutra of the Sixth Ancestor's Teaching Treasure (六祖大師法寶壇經, Zongbao recension, T48n2008), chapter on Sudden and Gradual (頓漸品); Huineng's teaching — self-nature awakens of itself, all at once, with no gradual steps. The core 'no gradual stages' sense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 有頓漸之異。故曰南頓北漸。非禪宗本有南北之號也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jingde-era Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), in an imperial dialogue. It explains 'Southern sudden, Northern gradual' (南頓北漸) as a difference between sudden and gradual (頓 / 漸) in leading people to awaken, not an original north-south division in Chan.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰丙丁童子來求火師於言下頓悟
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The 'fire-boy comes seeking fire' story (丙丁童子來求火); the monk awakens all at once at a single phrase ('at the words, suddenly awakened' 言下頓悟) — the living, on-the-spot use. Narrative frame, so MasterName=null.

Occurrences.Kwic: 理須頓悟，乘悟并銷，白雲斷處見明月；事在漸
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Guxue Zhe (古雪哲禪師語錄), a general address (普說); 'principle sudden, phenomena gradual' (理頓事漸) — principle must be awakened all at once, phenomena lie in the gradual. A master's own pairing of sudden (頓) and gradual (漸). Guxue Zhe (古雪哲) not in the canonical master list, so MasterName=null.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一漸修頓悟。二頓悟漸修。三漸修漸悟。四頓悟頓修。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Record of the Source-Mirror (宗鏡録), compiled by Yongming Yanshou, presents four propositions on sudden and gradual (頓漸四句), crossing sudden/gradual awakening with sudden/gradual refining. Locally this is a question and answer (問／答) citing the Laṅkāvatāra Scripture (楞伽經) on 'four graduals and four suddens' (四漸四頓); this passage does not attribute the formulation to Zongmi. MasterName is null.

Senses.Explanation: A paired contrast, literally 'sudden and gradual.' The term occurs 275 times in 104 allowed texts. The Platform Record reports that people spoke of Southern Huineng and Northern Shenxiu and therefore made a Southern/Northern division of sudden and gradual. Huineng's recorded correction is explicit: 'The teaching is originally one lineage; people are northern and southern. The teaching is one kind; seeing has slowness and speed. What is called sudden and gradual? The teaching has no sudden and gradual; people are sharp and dull, and therefore it is called sudden and gradual' (法本一宗，人有南北。法即一種，見有遲疾。何名頓漸？法無頓漸，人有利鈍，故名頓漸). Another recension puts it as 'seeing slowly is gradual, seeing quickly is sudden' (見遲即漸，見疾即頓), again followed by 'the teaching has no gradual and sudden' (法無漸頓). Later texts likewise say that sudden and gradual have no difference (頓漸無殊), or that whichever order is stated—'gradually refining, suddenly understanding' (漸修頓悟) or 'suddenly understanding, gradually refining' (頓悟漸修)—one must finally arrive personally once. The Record of the Source-Mirror enumerates four textual combinations: gradually refining and suddenly understanding, suddenly understanding and gradually refining, gradually refining and gradually understanding, and suddenly understanding and suddenly refining. That list records combinations of words; it does not override the Platform Record's direct correction or establish a hierarchy. The corpus contains five occurrences of 'the teaching has no sudden and gradual' (法無頓漸).
Senses.Note: The Platform Record locates slowness and speed in seeing and sharpness and dullness in people; later texts record the sudden/gradual combinations. In those cited combinations, 'refining' (修) translates the recorded graph literally.

Occurrences.Kwic: 人皆稱南能北秀，故有南北二宗頓漸之分，而學者莫知宗趣。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Platform Record. Huineng reports the division and directly corrects it by locating slowness and speed in people's seeing, not in the teaching.

Occurrences.Kwic: 法無頓漸，人有利鈍。迷即漸勸，悟人頓修。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An earlier Platform Record recension states that the teaching has no sudden and gradual and contrasts gradually urging the confused with the understanding person's sudden refining.

Occurrences.Kwic: 本來正教，無有頓漸，人性自有利鈍。迷人漸修，悟人頓契。自識本心，自見本性，即無差別，所以立頓漸之假名。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The later Platform Record recension calls sudden and gradual provisional names and again locates the difference in people rather than the teaching.

Occurrences.Kwic: 始知理事不二，頓漸無殊。且道：除卻頓漸，理事如何通信？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A later record says principle and events are not two and sudden and gradual do not differ, then asks how principle and events communicate when sudden and gradual are removed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 法即無頓漸，迷悟有遲疾，只此見性門，愚人不可悉。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Huineng's verse says the teaching has no sudden and gradual and that confusion and understanding have slowness and speed.
